title: Convert to Lowercase
directAnswer: For each char in 'A'..'Z', add 32 to its ASCII code; leave others unchanged. Or call `toLowerCase()`.
problemStatement: Given a string `s`, return it with every uppercase letter converted to lowercase. Non-letters are unchanged.
understanding: Mirror of to-uppercase: add 32 to uppercase letters.

approaches.name: ASCII shift
approaches.whenToMention: This is the standard, expected solution — lead with it.
approaches.explanation:
The mirror of to-uppercase: add 32 to an uppercase letter to get its lowercase form, since 'A'=65 and 'a'=97 differ by exactly 32.

**Why guard A–Z.** Only uppercase letters should change; the range check leaves digits, spaces, and symbols alone. Adding 32 to a non-letter would produce garbage.

**Direction.** Add 32 to go *down* to lowercase; subtracting would uppercase. Keeping the two directions straight (−32 up, +32 down) is the whole trick.

**Library note.** `toLowerCase()` handles locale and non-Latin scripts; the manual shift is the ASCII demonstration.
hints: Add 32 to A–Z letters; guard the range.
approaches.complexityReasoning: one range check and possible shift per character.

patternNote: A core fresher pattern: ASCII case shift. Master it on small inputs and it transfers to harder problems.
